name: vpa_pai
note: Ten VPaI loci reconstructed from RIMD 2210633 (NC_004603.1/NC_004605.1) and AQ3810 (GCA_000154045.1); VPaI-10 follows the RIMD T6SS region VP1387-VP1420 (VP1386 is absent from the RefSeq annotation). Built as one locus per island through the cluster pipeline; no typing scheme.

references.citation: Boyd EF, Cohen ALV, Naughton LM, Ussery DW, Binnewies TT, Stine OC, Parent MA. Molecular analysis of the emergence of pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus. BMC Microbiol. 2008;8:110.
references.note: Defines VPaI-1..VPaI-10, including the AQ3810 islands VPaI-8/VPaI-9 and the VPaI-9/VPaI-10 insertion-site comparison (Fig. S4).

references.citation: Hurley CC, Quirke A, Reen FJ, Boyd EF. Four genomic islands that mark post-1995 pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus isolates. BMC Genomics. 2006;7:104.

caveats: VPaI-1..7 coordinates follow RIMD 2210633; VPaI-8/9 follow the AQ3810 ORF descriptions. VPaI-10 is the RIMD T6SS region VP1387-VP1420 (VP1386 is absent from the RefSeq annotation): the 2008 paper shows the VPaI-9/VPaI-10 insertion-site comparison but does not publish a separate VPaI-10 coordinate table, so this boundary is the documented T6SS reconstruction.

Island presence and coverage are not a pathogenicity verdict: VPaIs can be partial, rearranged, or lost, and several islands occur in pre-1995 and environmental strains. Read the per-gene evidence, not just the locus coverage.
The panel carries no typing scheme; it answers which VPaIs are present and how completely, not which pathotype or serotype the isolate is.
